{{Short description|Theorem of gravity in cosmology}}
In [[cosmology]], the '''Gurzadyan theorem''', proved by [[Vahe Gurzadyan]],<ref name=Gurzadyan>{{cite journal | last=Gurzadyan |first=Vahe |authorlink=vahe Gurzadyan|title=The cosmological constant in McCrea-Milne cosmological scheme|journal=The Observatory|date= 1985|volume=105|pages=42–43|bibcode=1985Obs...105...42G}}</ref> states the most general functional form for the force satisfying the condition of identity of the gravity of the sphere and of a point mass located in the sphere's center. This theorem thus refers to the first statement of [[Isaac Newton]]’s <ref name="Newton philo">{{cite book|last=Newton|first=Isaac|title=Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica|url=https://archive.org/details/philosophinatur03newtgoog|date=1687|location=London|pages=Theorem XXXI}}</ref> [[shell theorem]] (the identity mentioned above) but not the second one, namely, the absence of gravitational force inside a shell.<ref>{{cite book | last1 =  Markoutsakis | first1 = M. |  year = 2021| title = Geometry, Symmetries, and Classical Physics: A Mosaic|series=|publisher= CRC Press | isbn =  978-0367535230 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 =  Phan | first1 = T.V. | year = 2025 | title = On the derivation of the cosmological Gurzadyan's theorem| url = | journal = Physics Education| volume = 61 | issue = 1 |  page = 015003| doi = 10.1088/1361-6552/ae153b | bibcode = 2026PhyEd..61a5003P | arxiv = 2504.02897 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 =  Carimalo | first1 = C. | year = 2026 |
title = A note on Gurzadyan theorem| arxiv = 2603.25323 }}</ref>

The theorem had entered and its importance for cosmology outlined in several papers <ref>{{cite journal | last1 =  Vedenyapin | first1 = V.V. | last2 = Fimin | first2 = N.N. | last3 = Chechetkin  | first3 = V.M. | year = 2021 | title = The generalized Friedmann model as a self-similar solution of Vlasov–Poisson equation system| url = | journal = European Physical Journal Plus | volume = 136 | issue = 6| page = 670 | doi = 10.1140/epjp/s13360-021-01659-7 | bibcode = 2021EPJP..136..670V}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Chardin | first1 = G. | last2 = Debois | first2 = Y.| last3 = Manfredi | first3 = G.| last4 = Miller | first4 = B.| last5 = Stahl | first5 = C.| year = 2021 | title = MOND-like behavior in the Dirac–Milne universe: Flat rotation curves and mass versus velocity relations in galaxies and clusters | url = | journal = Astronomy and Astrophysics| volume = 652 | issue = | page = 16 | doi = 10.1051/0004-6361/202140575 | arxiv = 2102.08834 | bibcode = 2021A&A...652A..91C}}</ref> as well as in [[shell theorem]].

== Formula and the cosmological constant ==
The formula for the force derived in  <ref name=Gurzadyan/> has the form
:<math> F = -\frac{G M m}{r^2} + \frac{\Lambda c^2 m r}{3}, </math>

where <math>G</math> and <math>\Lambda</math> are constants. The first term is the familiar law of universal gravitation, the second one corresponds to the [[cosmological constant]] term in [[general relativity]] and McCrea-Milne cosmology.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = McCrea | first1 = W.H. | last2 = Milne | first2 = E.A. | year = 1934 | title = Newtonian Universes and the curvature of space | url = | journal = Quarterly Journal of Mathematics | volume = 5 | issue = | page = 73 | doi = 10.1093/qmath/os-5.1.73 | bibcode = }}</ref>
Then the field is force-free only in the center of a shell but the confinement (oscillator) term does not change the initial <math> O(4) </math> symmetry of the Newtonian field. Also, this field corresponds to the only field possessing the property of the Newtonian one: the closing of orbits at any negative value of energy, i.e. the coincidence of the period of variation of the value of the radius vector with that of its revolution by <math> 2\pi </math> (resonance principle) .

== Consequences: cosmological constant as a physical constant ==

[[Einstein]] named the cosmological constant as a universal constant, introducing it to define the static cosmological model.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Einstein | first1 = A.  | year = 1917 | title = Kosmologische Betrachtungen zur allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie | url = | journal = Koniglich Preussische Akad. Der Wissenschaften | volume = 142| issue = | page = | bibcode = }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Einstein | first1 = A.  | year = 1918 | title = Bemerkung zu Herrn Schrödingers Notiz "Über ein Lösungssystem der allgemein kovarianten Gravitationsgleichungen", 3 Mär 1918 | url = | journal = Phys. Z. | volume = 19| issue = | page = 165 | bibcode = }}</ref> Einstein has stated:<ref>{{cite journal | last1 =  Einstein | first1 = A. | year = 1917 | title = Letter to Michele Besso | url =  https://einsteinpapers.press.princeton.edu/vol8a-doc/478 | journal = The Collected Papers of Albert Einstein | volume = 8 | issue = 308 | page = 404  |series= |publisher= Princeton University Press, 1998 | bibcode =}}</ref> “I should have initially set <math> \lambda = 0 </math> in Newton's sense. But the new considerations speak for a non-zero <math> \lambda </math>, which strives to bring about a non-zero mean density <math> \rho_0 </math> of matter.” This theorem solves that contradiction between “non-zero <math> \lambda </math>” and Newton's law.

From this theorem the cosmological constant <math> \Lambda </math> emerges as additional constant of gravity along with the Newton's gravitational constant <math> G </math>. Then, the cosmological constant is dimension independent and matter-uncoupled and hence can be considered even more universal than Newton's [[gravitational constant]].<ref name="GS1">{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Stepanian | first2 = A. | year = 2018 | title = Two fundamental constants of gravity unifying the dark matter and the dark energy | url = | journal = European Physical Journal C | volume = 78 | issue = | page = 632 | doi = 10.1140/epjc/s10052-018-6117-1 | bibcode = | doi-access = free | arxiv = 1807.11705 }}</ref>

For <math> \Lambda </math> joining the set of [[fundamental constants]] <math> (G, c, \hbar) </math>, the gravitational
Newton's constant, the [[speed of light]] and the [[Planck constant]], yields

:<math> [c]=LT^{-1},\quad [G]=M^{-1}L^3T^{-2},\quad [\hbar]=ML^{2}T^{-1},\quad [\Lambda]=L^{-2}, </math>

and a [[dimensionless quantity]] emerges for the 4-constant set <math>(G, \Lambda, c, \hbar)</math>
<ref name="GS2">{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Stepanian | first2 = A. | year = 2019 | title = Cosmological constant as a fundamental constant | url = | journal = European Physical Journal Plus | volume = 134 | issue = 3| page = 98 | doi = 10.1140/epjp/i2019-12532-3 | bibcode =| arxiv = 1901.10299 }}</ref>

:<math> I=\frac{c^{3a}}{\Lambda^a G^a \hbar^a}, </math>

where <math> a </math> is a [[real number]]. Note, no dimensionless quantity is possible to construct from the 3 constants <math> G, c, \hbar </math>.

This within a numerical factor, <math> a=1 </math>, coincides  with the [[information]] (or [[entropy]]) of [[de Sitter space|de Sitter]] event horizon 
<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gibbons | first1 = G.W. | last2 = Hawking | first2 = S.W. | year = 1977 | title = Cosmological event horizons, thermodynamics, and particle creation | url = | journal = Phys. Rev. D | volume = 15 | issue = 10| page = 2738 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2738 | bibcode = 1977PhRvD..15.2738G}}</ref>

:<math> I_{dS}= 3 \pi \frac {c^3}{\Lambda G \hbar}, </math>

and the [[Bekenstein Bound]]  <ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Bekenstein| first1 = J.D. | year = 1981 | title = Universal upper bound on the entropy-to-energy ratio for bounded systems | url = | journal = Phys. Rev. D | volume = 23| issue = 2| page = 287 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevD.23.287 | bibcode = 1981PhRvD..23..287B}}</ref>

:<math> I_{BB} =  \frac {3 \pi c^3}{\Lambda G \hbar ln 2}. </math>

=== Rescaling of physical constants ===

Within the [[conformal cyclic cosmology]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Penrose | first1 = R. | year = 2010 | title = Cycles of Time: An Extraordinary New View of the Universe | journal = Bodley Head, London | bibcode = 2010cten.book.....P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Penrose | first2 = R. | year = 2013 | title = On CCC-predicted concentric low-variance circles in the CMB sky  | journal = European Physical Journal Plus  | volume = 128 | issue = 2 | pages = 22 | arxiv = 1302.5162| bibcode = 2013EPJP..128...22G| doi = 10.1140/epjp/i2013-13022-4| s2cid = 55249027 }}</ref> this theorem implies that, in each aeon of an initial value of <math> \Lambda </math>, the values of the 3 physical constants will be eligible for rescaling fulfilling the dimensionless ratio of invariants with respect to the conformal transformation  <ref name="GS2" />

:<math> \tilde{g}_{\mu\nu}=\Omega^2 g_{\mu\nu}, </math>

Then the ratio yields

:<math> \frac{Q_{dS}}{Q_p}=m (\frac{c^3}{\hbar G \Lambda})^n = m I^n, \quad m,n \in \mathbb{R}, </math>

for all [[Physical quantity|physical quantities]] in [[Planck epoch|Planck]] (initial) and [[de Sitter space|de Sitter]] (final)  eras of the aeons, remaining invariant under conformal transformations.

== Inhomogeneous Fredholm equation==
This theorem, in the context of nonlocal effects in a system of gravitating particles, leads to the inhomogeneous [[Dirichlet]] [[boundary problem]] for the [[Poisson equation]]
<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Fimin | first2 = N.N. |last3=Chechetkin| first3=V.M.| year = 2023 | title = Cosmic voids and the kinetic analysis.II. Link to Hubble tension | url = | journal = Astronomy and Astrophysics| volume = 672 | issue = | page = A95 | doi = 10.1051/0004-6361/202346139 | arxiv = 2303.03194 | bibcode = 2023A&A...672A..95G}}</ref>

:<math> \Delta \Phi({\bf x}) = AN G_3 S_3^2
\bigg(\int_{y\in [0,\infty ]}\exp \big(-y^2/(2\theta) \big)y^2 dy
\bigg)\cdot \exp(-\Phi/\theta)-\frac{c^2\Lambda}{2},</math>

where  <math>R_\Omega</math> is the radius of the region,
:<math>A,\theta,R_\Omega \in {\mathbb R}^1</math>.
Its solution can be expressed in terms of the [[double layer potential]], which leads to an inhomogeneous nonlinear [[Hammerstein]] [[integral equation]] for the [[gravitational potential]]
:<math>  U({\bf x})=\widetilde{\lambda}  \widehat{\mathfrak G}({U})+
\alpha(\theta,\Lambda){\bf x}^2,~~
\widehat{\mathfrak G}({U})\equiv \int_{\Omega'} {\mathcal K}(|{\bf x}-{\bf x}'|)
\exp\big(-{U}({\bf x}')\big)d{{\bf x}'},</math>

:<math>
 U( {\bf x})\equiv (\Phi ({\bf x})-C_0)/\theta,~~
\widetilde{\lambda} \equiv \widetilde{\lambda_{II}}(\theta)
\equiv \frac{\lambda_{I}}{\theta}\exp(-C_0/\theta),~~
\alpha(\theta,\Lambda)= -\frac{\Lambda c^2}{12\theta}.</math>

This leads to a linear inhomogeneous 2nd kind [[Fredholm equation]]

:<math>
\phi({\bf x})=\lambda^{(0)} \int_{\Omega'}{\mathcal K}(|{\bf x}-{\bf x}'|)
  \phi({\bf x}')d{\bf x}' +\widehat{\beta}({\bf x}),
</math>

:<math> 
\widehat{\beta}({\bf x})\equiv  -\lambda^{(0)}\int_{\Omega'}
  {\mathcal K}(|{\bf x}-{\bf x}'|)\alpha |{\bf x}'|^2 d{\bf x}' -\alpha |{\bf x}|^2,
</math>

:<math>
{U}({\bf x})={U}_0-\phi ({\bf x}), ~~|{\phi }|\ll {U}_0;~~~
  \lambda^{(0)}\equiv-\widetilde{\lambda}\exp(-U_0). </math>

Its solution can be expressed in terms of the [[Resolvent formalism|resolvent]] <math>\Gamma</math> of the integral kernel and the non-linear (repulsive) term
:<math>  \phi ({\bf x}) = -\widehat\beta ({\bf x}) +\lambda^{(0)}\sum_{\bf n}
\langle -\widehat\beta ({\bf x}),\phi_{\bf n} \rangle \phi_{\bf n}\lambda_{\bf n}^{-1} + (\lambda^{(0)})^2\sum_{\bf n}\langle -\widehat\beta ({\bf x}),\phi_{\bf n} \rangle
\phi_{\bf n}\lambda_{\bf n}^{-1}(\lambda_{\bf n}-\lambda^{(0)})^{-1} =
</math>

:<math>
 -\widehat\beta ({\bf x}) +
\lambda^{(0)} \int_\Omega
\underbrace{
\bigg( {\mathcal K}({\bf x},{\bf x}') +
\lambda^{(0)}
\sum_{\bf n} \phi_{\bf n}({\bf x}) \phi_{\bf n}({\bf x}')
\lambda_{\bf n}^{-1}(\lambda_{\bf n}-\lambda^{(0)})^{-1}
\bigg)}_{\Gamma ({\bf x},{\bf x}',\lambda^{(0)})}
(-\widehat\beta ({\bf x}))d{\bf x}'. </math>

== Observational indications ==
The dynamics of groups and clusters of galaxies are claimed to fit the theorem,<ref name= "GS1" /><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | year = 2019 | title = On the common nature of dark matter and dark energy: galaxy groups | url = | journal = European Physical Journal Plus | volume = 134 | issue = 1| article-number = 14 | doi = 10.1140/epjp/i2019-12418-4 | bibcode = 2019EPJP..134...14G| arxiv = 1712.10014 }}</ref> see also.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Chardin | first1 = G. |display-authors=etal | year = 2021 | title = MOND-like behavior in the Dirac-Milne universe -- Flat rotation curves and mass/velocity relations in galaxies and clusters | url = | journal = Astronomy and Astrophysics | volume = 652 | issue = | page = 91 | doi = 10.1051/0004-6361/202140575 | bibcode = 2021A&A...652A..91C| arxiv = 2102.08834 }}</ref>
The possibility of two Hubble flows, a local one, determined by that formula, and a global one, described by [[Friedmann equations|Friedmann]]ian cosmological equations was stated in.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurzadyan | first1 = V.G. | last2 = Stepanian | first2 = A. | year = 2021 | title = Hubble tension and absolute constraints on the local Hubble parameter | url = | journal = Astronomy and Astrophysics| volume = 653 | issue = | page = A145 | doi = 10.1051/0004-6361/202141736 | arxiv = 2108.07407 | bibcode = 2021A&A...653A.145G}}</ref>

== Experimental consequences of the theorem ==
In  ref.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Fernandez-Melendez  | first1 = H.A. | last2 = Belyaev | first2 = A.|last3 = Gurzadyan|first3 = V.|last4 = Fuentes |first4 = I.| year = 2025 | title = Probing lambda-gravity with Bose-Einstein condensates | url = | journal =   Physical Review Research| volume = 7 | issue = 4 | article-number = L042051 | doi =  10.1103/7x8h-t1l9 | arxiv = 2409.19755 | bibcode = 2025PhRvR...7d2051F}}</ref> it is shown that the theorem provides a possibility to measure at a tabletop scale, using Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), the gravitational constant with an accuracy of up to 10^-17 N m^2/kg^2 and to establish an upper bound on the cosmological constant 10^-31 m^-2.
